proposals.before: Precious Origin 2, when the heir was born, he returned to the Pu mansion.
proposals.after: Precious Origin 2, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu mansion.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豫王 is Prince Yu, not a generic “heir”; the idiomatic gloss invents heirship.

proposals.before: In the second year of Precious Origin, when the Heir Apparent was born, he returned to the Pu residence.
proposals.after: In the second year of Precious Origin, when Prince Yu was born, he returned to the Pu residence.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豫王 should be rendered Prince Yu, not Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: Third month, renyin: the tomb of Prince Zhao was restored and staffed with guardians.
proposals.after: Third month, renyin: the tomb of the Qin Mourning Prince was restored and staffed with guardians.
proposals.reason: Chinese 秦悼王 is the Qin Mourning Prince; “Prince Zhao” drops the Qin title and misreads 悼.

proposals.before: Western tribesman Zha Qimizheng of the Zhaizi came in.
proposals.after: Zha Qimizheng, son of the western tribesman Zha Zhan, came in to submit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 瞎氊子瞎欺米征 means the son of 瞎氊 named 瞎欺米征, not “Zhaizi Zha Qimizheng.”

decisions.reason: Source 豫王生 names Prince Yu’s birth, not an unnamed heir; “the heir” invents heirship absent from the Chinese, and “Prince Yu” restores the titled person.
豫王 is the titled Prince Yu; “Heir Apparent” (太子) is not in the Chinese, so rendering him as Heir Apparent is a factual mistranslation.
秦悼王 is the Qin Mourning Prince (fief Qin + posthumous 悼); “Prince Zhao” drops 秦 and misreads 悼, so the proposed title is the accurate fix.
瞎氊子瞎欺米征 is kinship plus personal name—son of 瞎氊 named 瞎欺米征—and 內附 means submission; “Zhaizi” invents a tribe and omits the father–son link.
